question.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{6{x}^{3}-x}{{x}^{2}+1}.$
question.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{6{x}^{3}-x}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{6{x}^{3}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{x}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(6x-\frac{1}{x})}{(1+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(6x-0)}{(1+0)} \\  & =6{lim}_{x\to \infty }x \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.
